 Mfa No. 200346 of 2019
 Oral Judgment

(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE N.S.SANJAY GOWDA) "Whether the Commissioner for workman was justified in exonerating the liability of the Insurer on the ground that the driving licence of the deceased/employee was not produced and consequently the owner of the offending auto was liable for compensation ?"

It was the case of the claimants (who were the father and siblings of the deceased)
Afsar Shafiq Mulla, was killed in a motor vehicle accident when he was driving the auto rickshaw owned by the first respondent.
The accident occurred when the auto rickshaw was hit by an unknown vehicle.
The police registered a criminal case against an unknown vehicle and it is stated that subsequently a 'C' report was filed.

2. The claimants contended that the deceased was getting a monthly salary of `9,000/- under the first respondent and since he was an employee and the vehicle was covered under a comprehensive policy, the owner and NC: 2024:KHC-K:6927 consequently the Insurer would be liable for payment of compensation as provided under the Employees Compensation Act.
The Commissioner for Workman has accepted the fact that the deceased was an employee.
In fact, the first respondent admitted that the deceased was an employee.

The Commissioner for workman has also come to the conclusion that the deceased was aged 23 years, was drawing a monthly wages of `6,000/- and hence applied the relevant factor of 219.95 and held that the claimants are entitled to `6,74,850/-
(3,000/- x 219.95 + `15,000/- for funeral expenses).
3.
The Commissioner for workman has however thereafter taken the view that the claimants had not discharged the burden of proving that there was no violation of the policy conditions.

It has observed that it was essential for the claimants to produce the driving licence of the deceased-workman and since that was not produced, the Commissioner for workman has taken the NC: 2024:KHC-K:6927 view that there was violation of the policy conditions and fastened the liability on the owner of the vehicle.

4. The certified copy of the records which are furnished by the learned counsel for the claimants indicate that a legal notice was issued by the Insurer to the owner on 14.02.2019 (Ex.R4) calling upon the owner to produce the driving licence of the deceased-workman and the owner has responded with a reply stating that the vehicle was having a permit and he has also stated that the deceased was working under his employment and at the time of recruiting him as a driver, he had seen the driving licence of deceased Afsar Shafiq Mulla (workman) and only thereafter he had engaged him.
He has also gone on to state that he did make enquiries with the mother of deceased and she informed him that she was uneducated and did not know whereabouts of the driving licence.

sentences.text: It is therefore clear that there was no attempt by the owner to be silent on this issue and he has responded to the queries of the Insurer.

It may also be pertinent to state here that the police during the course of the investigation also did not come to the conclusion that the deceased was driving his auto rickshaw without a driving licence while filing the 'C' report which they would have definitely made a note of.

7. In the light of the statement of the owner and the fact that the police did not contend that the deceased did not have a driving licence, the argument of the Insurer that it will have to be held that the deceased did not have a driving licence cannot be accepted.

8. Consequently, the finding of the Commissioner for workman for exonerating the liability of the Insurer is set-aside and the Insurer is made liable for the compensation awarded by the Commissioner for workman.

9. If the Insurer is of the view that there was a breach of the policy conditions and deceased-workman did not possess a driving licence, it would be open for the Insurer to initiate appropriate proceedings against the NC: 2024:KHC-K:6927 owner and establish this fact and recover the compensation that it has paid to the claimants.
10. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the substantial question of law is answered in favour of the claimants.
